claims: Artemis I launched successfully on November 16, 2022, at 1:47 a.m. EST from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test.
Artemis I utilized the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is the world’s most powerful rocket.
Artemis I sent the Orion spacecraft around the Moon.
Artemis I lasted 25 days, 10 hours, and 53 minutes.
Artemis I splashed down on December 11, 2022.
The launch vehicle for Artemis I was Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1.
The payload for Artemis I was an uncrewed Orion capsule.
The key objective of Artemis I was to test the integrated systems of SLS and Orion for future crewed missions.
The launch of Artemis I occurred after several delays caused by tropical storms and hydrogen fuel leaks during previous countdown attempts.
Artemis I traveled approximately 1.4 million miles.
Artemis I reached a record distance of 270,000 miles from Earth.
The Orion capsule survived high-speed reentry at approximately 24,581 mph.
The Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II will carry four astronauts around the Moon.
Artemis III is planned to land the first woman and next man on the Moon.
